# Balance Theory raises USD $19m in Series A funding 

 Mon, 3rd Aug 2026 

 SEAN MITCHELL Publisher 

Balance Theory has raised USD $19 million in Series A funding in a round led by SYN Ventures.

DataTribe and TEDCO also participated, and cybersecurity executive Dan Burns joined the company as Executive chairman.

The Columbia, Maryland-based company sells software that helps chief information security officers and other security leaders manage cybersecurity investment decisions. ##### August 24, 2026 Craig Etkin

According to filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Fazeshift has raised $22 Million in new Series A funding. The federal securities law requires the notice to be filed by companies that have sold securities without registration under the Securities Act of 1933 in an offering made under Rule 504 or 506 of Regulation D or Section 4(a)(5) of the Securities Act. A company must file this notice within 15 days after the first sale of securities in the offering. For this purpose, the date of first sale is the date on which the first investor is irrevocably contractually committed to invest. Each issuer of securities that sells its securities in reliance on an exemption provided in Regulation D or Section 4(a)(5) of the Securities Act of 1933 must file this notice containing the information requested with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and with the state(s) requiring it. # Boom raises $15M Series A to bring fintech-style underwriting to rental housing 

Mary Ann Azevedo

Aug 18, 2026

It was 2020, and the COVID-19 pandemic had just hit. Rob Whiting was trying to help his brothers, both of whom had lost their jobs, find a more affordable rental.

“ As I went down the rabbit hole with them to help them on their application journey, I saw a lot of the pain points along the way,” Whiting recalls, “with one brother getting rejected for bad credit, including a mark on his credit report that was actually an error.”

Funding news· Published August 27, 2026

# Cloverleaf AI Raises $8.0M Series A for B2G Sales Intelligence

United States funding roundup, week of 2026-08-31: 30 verified rounds →

The RFP is already too late. Cloverleaf AI has raised $8.0M in a Series A round to push that argument further into the B2G sales market.

The company sells a sales-intelligence layer for government contracting, but it’s not another procurement database. It monitors public meetings, committees, and budget activity across 70,000-plus agencies and 200,000-plus identified speakers, then filters that noise into territory-specific signals for front-line sellers. The pitch: deals are won before the RFP drops, and sellers who shape procurement beat those who react to it. Cloverleaf says its approach has already produced results like Uber Transit reps generating over $1 million in pipeline per rep, per quarter. The fresh capital will go toward scaling that model, though the company didn’t specify which investors led or joined the round.
